articleTitle: Negative Impact of Approximated Signed Addition on Power Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: This paper presents evaluation results of a power- efficient JPEG compression circuit utilizing approximate computing. To achieve power efficiency, we replace summations in Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) with approximate additions that follow Carry-Maskable Adder (CMA) [1]. We evaluate both the quality of the compressed images and the power consumed by the circuit. However, we observed unexpected results where power consumption increased despite the use of approximation, contradicting our expectations. Our detailed investigations revealed that the addition of negative values in 2's complement representation led to an increased wasted power consumption. Although reports on investigations related to power reduction through approximate computing offer valuable insights for researchers in this field, they are often difficult to find. This paper shows the reasons why power reduction could not be achieved in this specific case study.

articleTitle: OpenFASOC: An Open Platform Towards Analog and Mixed-Signal Automation and Acceleration of Chip Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: The democratization of chip design is revolutionizing the field of analog and mixed-signal design by incorporating software practices into the development process. This has enabled automation tools for improving time to market and relieving the amount of engineering resources required for analog design: often the long pole in any chip tapeout. OpenFASOC, an open-source framework, has emerged as a suite of tools that automates the analog and mixed-signal design process. By leveraging a combination of design methodologies and tools, our framework strikes a balance between complexity and design performance. The framework employs a procedure-based approach with a cell-based flow using highly automated digital APR tools and a programmatic layout approach that offers greater layout reconfigurability. Circuit generators within OpenFASO C, such as voltage regulators, sensing, and interface circuits, are programmed to access a library of customized analog Aux Cells and seamlessly integrate them with digital components using a layout template. These procedure-based generators combine open-source tools with custom Python scripts to enable automated mixed-signal design. Furthermore, the custom design time of aux cells and other building blocks not amenable to the cell-based approach is addressed by leveraging programmatic layout, using GDSfactory-based Python scripts to codify layout into component classes.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Real Time Face Recognition For University Attendance System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: The current face recognition systems struggle with pose, lighting, and expression variations in real-world scenarios. To overcome these challenges, face recognition systems have to apply advanced algorithms and machine learning techniques to analyze and compare facial features. Several studies have proposed face recognition attendance systems based on real-time video processing using deep convolutional neural networks. These systems aim to address problems related to the accuracy rate, stability, and interface settings of the attendance system. In this study, we propose a deep learning approach for face recognition in real-time video data. We constructed a new dataset of real-time videos by automatically and incrementally detecting, labeling, tracing, and purifying faces. We then fine-tune a convolutional neural network with the labeled dataset. Our experimental results on a testing dataset from an attendance management system show that the fine-tuned network achieves an accuracy of 95.3%, outperforming the non-fine-tuned network, which has an accuracy of 81.4%.

articleTitle: Towards Polynomial Formal Verification of AI-Generated Arithmetic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: The popularity of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is growing in many domains. The designers have started to use AI in Electronic Design Automation (EDA) for the generation of highly optimized digital designs, particularly arithmetic circuits. The arithmetic blocks generated by deep and reinforcement learning usually outperform the generic architectures in terms of design characteristics such as area, delay, and power. As a result, it is expected that AI-generated arithmetic circuits will soon occupy an important place in many applications thanks to their highly efficient architectures. A crucial task after designing an arithmetic circuit, including AI-generated circuits, is verification. Formal methods can detect faulty designs before fabrication and prevent financial loss and disastrous consequences. Despite the huge progress of formal methods in verifying a wide variety of designs, their time and space complexity is not fully investigated, particularly for the AI-generated arithmetic circuits. In this paper, we calculate the complexity bounds for formal verification based on Binary Decision Diagrams (BDDs) when they are used to ensure the correctness of general prefix adders. We prove that the Polynomial Formal Verification (PFV) of a prefix adder is possible independent of the prefix tree structure. Our proof is valid for both regular prefix adders generated by known algorithms and irregular prefix adders generated by AI.

articleTitle: Hybrid Genetic Algorithm Random Forest algorithm (HGARF) for improving the missing value Imputation in Hepatitis Medical Dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: It has always been difficult to make an exact prediction when there are many missing numbers in the data collection. To solve this problem, the majority of hybrid models either removed the absent cases from the data collection or used a default method to fill in the blanks. In the study described in this article, an improved genetic algorithm metaheuristics-based forecasting model is suggested to forecast the number of confirmed instances of hepatitis. The Random Forest's characteristics are chosen using the improved genetic method, which also improves the efficiency and accuracy of the prediction model overall. On standard medical data sets for Hepatitis from the UCI Repository of Machine Learning, the effectiveness of the suggested model as a predictive categorization system is examined. In addition to accuracy, sensitivity, specificity; and the area under ROC are also computed. The proposed method was contrasted with various current state-of-the-art approaches that were examined in the same setting and using the same datasets. Based on the outcomes of the simulations and the comparative analysis that was done, it was found that the suggested hybrid method outperformed more complex ones with an accuracy of 93.91% and that it could be applied to other prediction models.

articleTitle: Target Voltage Control Approach for Active Distribution System Based on PV Active and Reactive Powers Nodal Prices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: Distribution systems with renewable-based distributed energy resources often face several voltage problems, including voltage fluctuations and rise. These problems make it difficult for system operators to control voltage effectively. Therefore, operators of distribution systems should consider these issues in future grid planning. In this paper, a promise voltage control technique is developed, referred to as the target voltage control (TVC) approach. The objective of the TVC approach is to maximize the distributed energy resources powers, decrease the profit unfairness among the prosumers, and enhance the grid voltage quality by mitigating the voltage rise problems. The proposed approach is unique in its ability to significantly reduce the control performance degradation that results from infrequent data exchange among the controlled agents. Through simulated case studies of a 38-node distribution test feeder with several photovoltaic sources, it has been demonstrated that the proposed TVC approach can effectively achieve the desired objective with low-frequency communication data exchange.

articleTitle: Effect of PV Soiling on Day-ahead Scheduling of a Grid Integrated Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: This Globally grid integrated Solar PV generation is getting a good momentum in depleting fossil fuel generation which is evident from GW level plant installations. Soiling in such SPV plants is established to be one of the predominant agents which reduce generation to a great extent. This will affect the short term and long-term operation scheduling of a power system. In this paper, a grid-integrated microgrid has been considered to assess the changes in the short-term day ahead operation scheduling of a microgrid considering the PV soiling. The actual field data are collected from the microgrid at Indian Institute of Science and Technology (IIEST), Shibpur to validate the propositions. It is observed that the daily soiling loss becomes 5% to 35% in this location. The operating cost is increased by ~12% alongwith changes in the operating pattern of the microgrid from zero soiling to actual soiled condition.

articleTitle: Influence of Kerr Nonlinearity on Dispersion-Shifted and Dispersion-Flattened Silica Fibers: An Accurate Finite Difference Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: This research provides a useful study of the dispersion properties exhibited by standard silica fiber in the presence of Kerr nonlinearity based on our developed code using Finite Difference Method (FDM). The numerical results yield the Zero Dispersion Wavelength (ZDW) shifting towards the 1550 nm wavelength window by varying maximum input power from 1 mW to 20 mW. We also demonstrate the flattening of the total dispersion around the ZDW. With maximum input powers of 25 mW, 50 mW and 115 mW, we achieve the flat total dispersion values between 0±1.50 ps/km-nm over the bandwidths of 219 nm, 451 nm, and 527 nm respectively.

articleTitle: Temperature Sensor Circuit for a Wearable Perspiration Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: In this work, a prototype system has been designed with a 0.18-µm CMOS technology to capture perspiration rate in daily life. To calculate an amount of perspiration, a temperature sensor is necessary concurrently with a relative humidity sensing. The designed temperature sensor consists of 8-bit binary digital-to-analog converter and an analog front-end circuit for thermistors. The designed circuits for temperature and humidity sensors have successfully verified.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of All-Fiber Electric Field Sensing Device
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: This report our experimental demonstration of all-fiber electric field sensing device based on a three mirror Fabry-Perot arrangement using the fiber-cantilever beam deflection configuration with an optimized composition of cobalt-doped bismuth ferrite nanoparticles as probe material. The reflected fiber-exit beam is modulated with an electric field. Our Fabry-Perot transmission analysis with a cantilever-deflection host yields precise results experimentally obtained, showing the efficacy of this new concept.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Grid integrated BESS Solar PV System to Supply Critical Loads under Grid Outage Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: Fossil fuel consumption has a negative impact on the environment, for which usage of solar energy is getting momentum. The fundamental issue with grid integration of solar energy is that today's on-grid inverters have the property of requiring a reference signal from the grid. If a grid outage occurs, the on-grid inverter stops functioning because it would not receive any grid reference signal and all the generated power from plant remains unutilized and continuous power supply to critical load is interrupted. This paper proposes an innovative network and control arrangement enabling the generated PV power to be utilized at the moment of a daytime grid outage. When PV doesn't provide enough power during the day, vital loads are powered by the battery, and when there is grid outage at night, battery power is used to power critical loads. This includes an on-grid and an off-grid inverter connected in parallel such that off-grid one takes the critical loads when the on-grid one goes to sleep mode. A fast switching technique maintains continuous supply to the critical load after a grid failure and it keeps the output voltage constant with the fluctuation of the load. At first the proposed inverter has been designed on PSIM platform and simulation is done. Then a hardware prototype is fabricated and tested in the laboratory to validate its functionality.

articleTitle: Electrothermal modeling of Multilayer Graphene Nanoribbon (MLGNR) Interconnect considering Energy-per-Layer Screening
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: An explicitly precise energy-per-layer screened electrothermal interconnect model has been developed in this paper that contemplates the impact of Fermi screening (FSc) with temperature for different intercalation doped top contact multilayer graphene nanoribbon (TC-MLGNR). Moreover, a comparative investigation is carried out to examine the impact of temperature upon the resistance of the effective number of layers <tex>$(R_{\mathrm{L}_{-}\text{efct}})$</tex> participating in current conduction. It has been observed that the thermal response considering FSc is different for each layer. Moreover, with FSc, the rate of change of resistance with temperature is different for different intercalated TC-MLGNR. The finite difference between effective resistance considering with <tex>$(R_{\text{efct}_{-}\text{Efs}})$</tex> and without <tex>$(R_{\text{efct}_{-}\mathrm{E}\mathrm{f}})$</tex> FSc shows linear distribution over the chip operating temperature range, which supposedly put forth a significant footprint on the existing self-heating models. Hence, it is pertinent that by incorporating FSc, our proposed model, flow through the electrothermal design of GNR interconnects in upcoming VLSI circuits.

articleTitle: Review on DMTFET based Biosensor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: Biosensors, also known as biological sensors, have become increasingly important in our daily lives. The increasing number of new diseases has necessitated the use of biosensors to detect the type of bacteria or foreign things that are causing the ailments. Using biosensors, various types of germs and other bio-molecules in a wide variety of sizes can be easily detected and recognized, allowing for further treatment. As a result, many devices are continuously being researched for the manufacture of biosensors. FET or Field Effect Transistors-based biosensors have received a lot of attention among the available devices; the primary reasons for this are their high detection ability, good sensitivity, low cost, and easy fabrication compatibility with CMOS technology. Although FET-based biosensors have many advantages, they also have several limitations. Among the downsides, short channel effects (SCEs) and theoretical limitations on a sub-threshold swing (SS>60m V/dec) limit FET sensitivity, and thermionic emissions cause massive power consumption, resulting in device inefficiency. To address these issues, researchers looked to newer technologies, which led to the development of TFETs, or Tunnel FETs. TFETs have many advantages over FETs, including low power consumption, carrier band-to-band tunneling, and minimal threshold swing. There are numerous configurations linked to the efficient operation of TFETs, and this paper provides a detailed study of dielectric-modulated TFET-based biosensors. This publication also describes the quantitative parameters analysis, such as the device's sensitivity and other characteristics that lead to improved and more efficient device functioning. Furthermore, approaches for improving the device and future scopes are described at the end of this work.

articleTitle: Dynamic Frequency Control of a Low Inertia Microgrid using Virtual Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: Conventional synchronous generator has the ability to control system frequency fluctuation because of its large inertia and damping ability. Due to influx of renewable sources in modern power systems low inertia distributed power generation sources are becoming predominant. The variability of these sources negatively impacts the frequency stability of such systems under normal and abnormal conditions. Due to usage of low inertia sources e.g., inverter-based systems, it becomes difficult to arrest the frequency deflection. In this paper, to include the effect of inertia, a Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) control technology is proposed. This research suggests an adaptive damping coefficient and moment of inertia control technique to address this shortcoming. A mathematical model for the proposed VSG is developed and analyzed. A simulation model is presented in MATLAB/Simulink platform to confirm the working behavior of proposed VSG control system. The results obtained are quite encouraging.

articleTitle: Study of PbS Nanomaterial Sensitized ZnO based Solar Cell using SCAPS-1D Simulator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: PbS is generally used as the preferred material for sensitizing layer in solar cells due to its wide range of band-gap tunability. As the light absorption in in sensitizing layer of solar cell depands on the band gap of the material, hence nano-crystalline PbS has a wider range of light absorption starting from the UV up to the NIR regions of the solar spectrum. In the present study we have simulated a FTO/ZnO/PbS/Al type structure using SCAPS-1D simulator, and the Current density curve is obtained for voltage characteristics is studied. With an aim of studying the effect of the thickness of the sensitization layer on the working of solar cell, the thickness of the nano-crystalline PbS layer is varied and the values of the essential solar cell factorsare acquired for the simulated solar cell.

articleTitle: Neural Network Architectures for Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: This paper presents the architectural design and implementation of neural networks (NNs) for integrated circuit design. The architecture consists of the adder, multiplier, and rectified linear unit (ReLU) blocks. Three architectures (i) single-in single-out (SISO), (ii) multiple-in single-out (MISO), and (iii) multiple-in multiple-out (MIMO) are developed. In NNs, weight values are required, fed from a manually generated memory. The weight values were prepared by training the NNs model on software. Finally, the SISO, MISO, and MIMO neural-networks were taped out.

articleTitle: A comprehensive review on ReRAM-based accelerators for deep learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: The current success of AI-artificial intelligence is mainly due to the ubiquity of deep learning network in numerous applications such as language processing, object detection, image classification etc. Consequently, many research works are developing memristor-based accelerators to improve the effectiveness of existing deep learning networks. One of the design aspects of accelerators is to achieve computation near-memory to overcome the memory wall and von Neumann bottleneck. The requirements of deep neural networks to perform complex computations are increasing faster than the improvement in recent CMOS- based hardware. To achieve this, researchers have investigated a variety of crossbar topologies based on non-volatile memory to attain complex operations and increase on-chip storage density. This paper presents a comprehensive review of accelerators designed using non-volatile memories. The key challenge with the NVM-based crossbar is the extensive range of non-idealities at the device and circuit levels. Many research works have proposed a framework for mitigating non-idealities. This paper also reviews accelerators designed for modelling non-idealities in the NVM crossbar.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Switching Performance of Self-Heating Effect on SiC-based Power-Electronic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: The high-frequency power-switch-driven self-heating effect on the conduction and switching performance of the 4H- Silicon Carbide (SiC) DMOSFET-based general-purpose inverter stack (GPIS) circuit has been investigated through an integrated device and circuit simulation approach. This study presents the empirical significance of the blocking switch with an embedded body diode in the H-bridge converter circuit on switching and conduction loss with instantaneous temperature rise. It has been explored that an insignificant self-heating effect on the switching performance and non-negligible post-switching body-diode carried conduction loss rise with the real-time increase of device temperature during circuit operation.

articleTitle: Design of High Gain Low-Noise Amplifier at X-Band Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: In this work, a high gain, low noise amplifier (LNA) at 10 GHz has been designed. For this, a dual-stage cascode topology has been used in a commercial 180nm CMOS process. Also, this cascode structure has been cascaded with another similar cascode stage to achieve high gain, and the inductive peaking procedure has been implemented in both loads of the 1st and 2nd stages to improve gain and bandwidth. The input reflection coefficient (S11) is about −14 dB for the frequency of 10 GHz. The simulated outcomes show that the gain of the LNA is greater than 25dB, and the noise figure is about 4.31 dB. Also, here with this topology, the difference between the noise figure (NF) and the minimum noise figure (NFmin) has been taken into significant focus.

articleTitle: Design of low-power and high-performance 10 nm SRAM using Electrostatically doped TMD TFET
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: In this work, a comparison of the Electrostatically Doped Tunnel Field-Effect Transistor (EDTFET) with Transition Metal Dichalcogenide (TMD) as channel material and Si MOSFET-based Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) has been carried out at the circuit level using a Verilog-A interface. A 6T SRAM has been implemented in Cadence Virtuoso for this comparison. It has been observed that the EDTFET SRAM demonstrates superior performance in terms of HOLD, WRITE, and READ noise margins and delay, while maintaining power dissipation at a comparable level. The HOLD, WRITE, and READ noise margins of the EDTFET are 0.2313 V, 0.06 V, and 0.2824 V, respectively, which are 33.93 %, 20 %, and 31.96 % higher than the HOLD, WRITE, and READ noise margins of the Si MOSFET-based SRAM. The delay achieved by the EDTFET-based SRAM is 4 decades lower than that of the Si MOSFET-based SRAM.

articleTitle: Fighting Deepfakes by Detecting DCT Frequency Anomalies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: The recent widespread use of deep learning has led media synthesis and manipulation to reach previously unheard-of degrees of realism. Deepfake has been a standard media manipulation tool adopted in synthesis of fake media, including videos, images, and audio recordings. Deepfake technology today has reached a potential to tremendously impact the trustworthiness of multimedia data considerably. This has significant ramifications for people, organizations, and society at large. Current literature presents numerous cases of fake news to sway public opinion as well as personal defamation cases. In this paper, we investigate the frequency domain spectrum of deepfake videos and propose the exploitation of high-frequency DCT coefficients gathered from videos to serve as a distinctive fingerprint. We construct a resilient model capable of distinguishing between pristine videos and its deepfake derivative, based on variance of differences between consecutive video frames' DCT coefficients.

articleTitle: A New Approach of Designing All-fiber Band Rejection Filter based on Multimode-Single mode-Multimode Fiber Concatenated Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: Our proposal introduces a novel all-fiber band rejection filter that utilizes a concatenated structure known as multimode-single mode-multimode (M-S-M). This filter design incorporates two identical multimode fibers (MMFs) and a conventional single-mode fiber (SMF) with a very short length, which is spliced between the MMFs. A notable interference loss is observed as a result of the core diameter difference between the MMF and SMF. Through systematic adjustments of the fibers' parameters in the M-S-M configuration, we demonstrate that the interference loss within the device can be effectively utilized as a band rejection filter.

articleTitle: Photodiode and Analog-Front-End Circuit Design for Wearable Vital Sensing System with Fiber-Bragg-Grating Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: A prototype of wearable vital sensing system has been developed with Fiber-Bragg-Gratings senor and 180-nm CMOS image sensor process chip. The system can acquire vital signs by capturing reflecting light with a photodiode. The designed test chip contains two types analog-front-end circuit. The feasibility for a vital sensing was verified with measurements with both of current-voltage conversion type and integral analog-to-digital convertor type.

articleTitle: Security Attacks on Social Networking: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: Social networking sites allow people to share their information and help to create social contact. Nowadays, it has become an integral part of human life. The first thing any person does just after waking up is checking notifications from various social media platforms they have an account on. Hence, we all can imagine the importance of social networking on human beings. However, sharing information and making contact with the unknown are the key concerns of security in social networks. Now it is very much possible for common men to be tricked into traps by attackers. This paper focuses on different aspects of social networking securities and explains the various categories of online attacks possible on social networking. Moreover, this survey tries to find out the drawbacks and limitations in the literature along with a brief analysis of the security attacks on social networks.

articleTitle: Memristor based In-Memory Computing for Edge AI Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: Cloud computation overload significantly reduces with the improvement in the computation capabilities of edge devices. The development of sensor devices and networks connected through the internet results in a continuous increase in the volume and variability of data. Processing-in-memory can significantly reduce the data processing challenges utilizing memristor-based neural network hardware for edge devices. In this paper, we have briefly reviewed various materials and logic styles for memristor-based computations. Various synapse structures using memristor and different neuron cells are presented, which shows superiority over CMOS-based neural networks. The comparative discussion evaluates the performance of various non-volatile memory technologies for edge applications.

articleTitle: Resource-efficient VLSI Architecture of Softmax Activation Function for Real-time Inference in Deep Learning Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: The Softmax activation function layer is the output layer in various Deep Learning (DL) models for multi-class classification applications. It computes the probability values for each input entry to the layer and represents the degree of confidence. The nonlinearity of the softmax function poses a challenge of increased hardware complexity. Therefore, the proposed VLSI architecture of the softmax activation function aims to reduce hardware resources with minimal loss in accuracy. The proposed architecture utilizes an optimized design of a ROM-based exponential unit for exponentiation and a Newton-Raphson iterations-based division by reciprocation unit for division operation. The proposed architecture is evaluated on Xilinx's Kirtex-7 KC705 FPGA Evaluation Platform, achieving LUTs 1.44 - 11.61 × lesser than the other state-of-the-art architectures on the MNIST dataset.

articleTitle: Generation of Broadband Supercontinuum by a So-designed Silicon on Insulator (SOI) Rectangular Buried Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: The generation of supercontinuum in near-infrared regions is a very useful application in the domain of telecommunication. Here we numerically study the generation of supercontinuum using an SOI rectangular core buried waveguide. From our simulation, we find that using an un-chirped 1.4 KW input Gaussian pulse with a temporal width of 200 fs results in a broadband intensity spectrum of wavelength span 1.275 to 1.912 µm covering the entire communication band starting from O to L, which makes it potentially applicable in the field of communication and many more.

articleTitle: Implementation of Area Efficient Adders for Inexact Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: In recent years the archetype of approximate computing is very much highlighted for satisfying the never ending requirement of decreasing power utilization in modern electronic devices. The application domain of multimedia signal processing with complex computations represents a typical trade-off between power and quality in inexact computing. Adder is backbone of digital VLSI circuits. For high mathematical complexity applications, approximate adders are proposed as a feasible solution in this paper, which can give a better trade-off with accuracy in terms of energy consumed, area occupied and delay. We present in this work that the efficiency of the Approximate Ripple Carry Adder (ARCA) 75%, 50% and 25% accuracy is achieved with better speed, reduced area and power consumption as a trade-off. Our work reflects the fact that by sacrificing efficiency to a tolerable limit we reduce area as compared with the existing conventional RCAs.

articleTitle: A Multiphase Low Phase-Noise DCO based on Self-Timed Ring Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: This paper presents multiphase low-phase noise digitally controlled oscillators (DCOs) based on C-element self-timed ring oscillator (C-STRO) implementation. The proposed C-STRO outperforms traditional ring oscillators (ROs) by reducing gate delay variations and white noise. This results in improved phase noise performance and multiple high-resolution phases with low jitter. The C-STRO-based DCO results show that it maintains a similar size and tuning range to the conventional RO while improving phase noise. The C-STRO has several advantages over traditional STROs, including higher phase resolution, lower power consumption, reduced clock jitter, simple circuit structure, and compatibility with standard CMOS technologies. The DCO has been implemented in 65 nm CMOS technology. The proposed architecture generates a tuning range from 500MHz to 4GHz. Phase noise at 1 MHz frequency offset is from −92dBc/Hz to −105dBc/Hz. Figure of Merit (FoM) calculated as −166.2dBc/Hz, an improvement of approximately 4 dB from previously published work.

articleTitle: Design of an Optimized Micro-heater using Soft-Computing Tools for Low Temperature Gas Sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: The paper deals with the optimization of power consumption in a micro-heater, (ZnO Sensing element) developed on a silicon wafer. Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) Algorithm have used to get optimum power consumption value of a micro-heater. Three parameters of the micro-heater such as the depth of oxide layer (‘dsio2’), the surface area of the membrane (‘Ah’) and the temperature of the sensing element (‘Th’) have been used as input parameters for this purpose. The output function of the sensor's equation for optimization is the power consumption. The algorithms have implemented on MATLAB software.The Intellisuite 8.2 software is used as simulation software for simulating the device. It is observed that ABC based optimization method provides superior result (0.890W) compared to the GA based optimization method (1.117W).

articleTitle: Switching Activity Reduction in Graphene PN Junction Circuits using Circuit Re-structuring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: Graphene PN Junction (GPNJ) logic circuits received significant attention from the researchers thanks to the availability of electrostatically doped graphene PN Junction (GPNJ) device- a promising one for designing low-power, high-speed circuits. Several design approaches for GPNJ logic circuits realizing important arithmetic and arbitrary Boolean functions exist in literature. However, no detailed evaluations of the resulting circuit complexities with respect to relevant cost metrics are reported. It remains open, how do we synthesize GPNJ logic circuits with minimal switching activity, an essential cost metric influencing the dynamic power dissipation in the resulting circuits. In this paper, we introduce a synthesis approach for GPNJ logic circuits that interconnects a set of GPNJ devices in parallel. Such parallel circuit structures ensure the reduction of switching activity in the resulting GPNJ logic circuits. To the best of our knowledge, so far only one research work discussed the computation of switching activity of GPNJ logic circuits. Experimental evaluations confirm that an average 67.35% reduction in switching activity can be achieved using the proposed approach over the existing one.

articleTitle: Design of CMOS Memristor Emulator and Logic Gates For Neuromorphic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: In this work, we have emulated the memristor characteristics using CMOS technology. Different topologies of the CMOS memristor have been realized. The design of an optimized memristor emulator circuit uses only three MOSFET transistors and a MOS cap. The proposed emulator exhibits similar nonlinear voltage-current characteristics and hysteresis as memristors. Previously developed memristor emulator circuits were complex because they required a large number of transistors and other blocks to achieve the desired memristor-like behavior. Our proposed memristor emulator will consume low power and have a small chip area. The memristor circuit simulation was performed using HSPICE at the 90nm CMOS technology node. The simulation result shows that the delay and power consumption in 4-NMOS-based and 1-NMOS/2-PMOS-based memristor emulators are lower than other existing emulator topologies. Furthermore, memristor emulator circuits have been used to realize the 2-input OR and 2-input AND gates. The development of CMOS based memristor emulator circuits and logic gates will pave the way for neuromorphic and machine learning circuits.

articleTitle: EMOTION RECOGNITION FROM EEG SIGNALS BASED ON OPTIMIZATION OF MUTUAL INFORMATION
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: Emotion is a mental state of feelings triggered by internal or external stimuli and sometimes by both. In general Mutual Information (MI) between the subjects' EEG signal energy and a manual score of emotion (MSE) is less which makes the prediction task difficult. In this work, to enhance the accuracy, nonlinear prediction methods are applied to normalized data sets with two classes of emotion where an emotional template has been designed based on adaptive bins for the classification of emotion. In this work, Subject-dependent emotion prediction has been explored extensively. We found that the MI or dependence between the data set and the MSE is the key to higher prediction accuracies. So it is important and necessary to find dimensions in signal space along which the MI between EEG signal energy and MSE is optimum. In particular, a gradient ascent algorithm has been used to find such dimensions in the multi-channel EEG signal energy space. In this current research, we have achieved high prediction accuracies of 86.95% to 90.23% for two classes of emotion in subject-dependent classification. The merit of the proposed approach is that it is devoid of any assumptions and user-based choice of parameters. we propose a simple but efficient emotion recognition approach using DEAP database.

articleTitle: Intelligent Transportation of Heterogeneous droplets in DMFB: A Preferential Deviation Based Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Devices, Circuits and Systems (ISDCS)
abstract: In order to enhance the performance of DMFBs, the parallel routing of droplets plays a crucial role. By implementing this approach in a single bio-assay, we can effectively optimize the latest arrival time. However, the various fluidic constraints present on DMFB platform raise different challenges such as collisions and contaminations, especially when dealing with heterogeneous droplet routing. Therefore, it becomes imperative to devise an efficient algorithm that not only satisfies all the constraints but also minimizes issues like stalling, collisions, and contaminations caused by parallel routing. By tackling these obstacles head-on, we can significantly improve the overall efficiency and reliability of DMFBs. In this work, we propose an algorithm for heterogeneous droplet transportation. The proposed intelligent deviation preference scheme serves as a valuable tool in enhancing the overall performance and reliability of the system, allowing for seamless parallel routing and improved cell utilization with latest arrival time.
